To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we observe temporal quantum fluctuations of the Stokes intensity in stimulated Raman amplification, and that (2) we describe them by a theory based on the concept that a pulse is a superposition of coherent temporal modes.

we have experimentally observed the quantum fluctuations of the Stokes intensity generated by stimulated Raman scattering in a nonlinear fiber, and that we have developed a theory that describes the quantum statistics of the Stokes intensity in the linear regime.

we observe temporal quantum fluctuations of the Stokes intensity produced in stimulated Raman backscattering, that we develop a theory to describe these fluctuations, and that the theory allows to predict the probability for generating solitons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of light pulses in the linear regime and the propagation of light in the nonlinear regime.
the study of the temporal fluctuations of the intensity and phase of light pulses produced by a laser beam in a Raman medium.
the generation of coherent Stokes pulses by means of stimulated Raman Scattering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work has shown the possibility of using a simple and efficient method to describe the temporal quantum fluctuations in stimulated raman scattering.
the present paper presents the first experimental evidence of the temporal quantum fluctuations of the Stokes light pulses in the linear regime.

the present results show that the coherent-modes approach is an efficient tool to describe the quantum fluctuations of the light intensity produced in the linear propagation of light in a medium exhibiting a nonlinear response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temporal modes concept allows a simple and accurate description of the temporal quantum noise in a wide range of experimental conditions.

we have demonstrated that the quantum fluctuations of a laser beam in the linear regime can be used as a source of entangled photon pairs, which is a key ingredient in quantum cryptography and quantum computation.
the coherent temporal mode concept is useful for understanding and predicting the quantum noise properties of the output of stimulated Raman amplifiers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the temporal coherence of the Stokes field, and thus its ability to form solitons in the nonlinear regime, is determined by the coherence of the pump field.
the temporal quantum fluctuations of the Stokes pulse can be described with the same number of random variables as in the case of the pump.
the quantum nature of light is a crucial ingredient in the formation of solitons in the nonlinear propagation of light pulses.
